output.name: Ketsa
output.myth: In the hungry winter the goats came in past the door-stones one by one. Ketsa, a grey nanny with a torn ear, would not come. She stood on the cliff edge with the salt wind in her coat and bleated at the byre until the men gave up. Tavo came up laughing and tried to push her off. She held her feet and butted him back. Tavo cannot be bargained with, so he laughed harder and went off down the wind. Then Hesk, who keeps count, came to the edge. She did not scold. She lifted the goat to the north end of the Spindle, where nothing sets, and hung her there. Morath, the Smoke That Stops, hangs a hand-span west of her, and Halun, the Gull Who Waited, watches from the east, knowing what waiting costs. Now every hearth-door can find her from the step. When the wind is wrong at night she is looking for the door she left, and Hesk keeps her lamp lit so she will not be lost. Mend your nets, child, and do not stand so long on the edge.
output.finding: Find Morath, the Smoke That Stops, on the Spindle, then go a hand-span east of it to where nothing sets and you will see Ketsa hanging there.
